relationship_types.layered-on-top-of: Source category sits architecturally above target. Source requires target to function.
relationship_types.feeds-into: Source category produces data or context that target category consumes.
relationship_types.executes-on: Source category agents/tools perform operations on target category protocols.
relationship_types.submitted-via: Source category produces transactions that target category submits to the network.
relationship_types.wraps: Source category provides a UI or SDK abstraction over target category functionality.
relationship_types.contextualizes: Source category exposes target category's capabilities to AI agents.
relationship_types.signs-for: Source category creates signed payloads that target category submits.
relationship_types.schedules: Source category manages execution scheduling and retry for target category work.
relationship_types.delegates-signing-to: Source category determines WHAT transaction to create; target category performs the cryptographic signing. The reasoning layer delegates key authority to the wallet layer.

relationships.description: ERC-4337 infrastructure (bundlers, paymasters) sits architecturally above wallet infrastructure. Account abstraction adds programmable rules and gas sponsorship to the underlying keypair managed by a wallet.
relationships.workflow_context: In a gasless onboarding flow: Privy (wallet-infrastructure) creates the embedded wallet; Pimlico (account-abstraction) sponsors the first transaction gas. AA requires a wallet to exist first.

relationships.description: Chain data infrastructure provides the onchain state signals that agent reasoning layers consume to make decisions. Without chain data, agents have no environmental awareness.
relationships.workflow_context: In a Solana trading agent: Helius (chain-data) streams onchain events via webhooks; the Vercel AI SDK agent (agent-framework) receives those events and decides what action to take.

relationships.description: Market data providers supply price signals, OHLCV, and portfolio context that trading agents use for decision-making.
relationships.workflow_context: In a trading agent: Birdeye (market-data) provides price and wallet P&L context; the agent framework processes that data alongside chain events to reason about trade decisions.

relationships.description: Farcaster social graph data feeds into agent reasoning for social-context-aware actions — follow graphs, cast content, notification triggers.
relationships.workflow_context: In a Farcaster AI agent: Neynar (social-layer) provides cast data and social graph; the agent framework processes that content and decides what onchain action to trigger.

relationships.description: AI agents use agent frameworks to reason about and dispatch transactions to DeFi protocols. The agent framework decides WHAT to do; the DeFi protocol defines the available operations.
relationships.workflow_context: In a trading agent: the agent framework determines a swap is warranted; it calls Jupiter (defi-protocol) to compute the optimal route and construct the transaction.

relationships.description: Agents query chain-data tools directly to read account state, verify transaction outcomes, and confirm execution results.
relationships.workflow_context: After submitting a trade, the agent framework reads Helius (chain-data) to confirm the transaction landed and update internal state.

relationships.description: Transactions constructed by DeFi protocol SDKs (e.g., Jupiter swap routes) are submitted to the network via execution infrastructure (e.g., Jito bundles). The protocol computes what to do; execution determines how to submit it with MEV protection.
relationships.workflow_context: Jupiter (defi-protocol) computes the optimal swap route and outputs a transaction. Jito (execution) wraps that transaction in a bundle and submits it with priority landing guarantees.

relationships.description: Wallet infrastructure signs transactions; execution infrastructure submits signed transactions to the network. These are adjacent pipeline stages — signing is wallet's job, submission is execution's job.
relationships.workflow_context: In an autonomous trading agent: Turnkey (wallet-infrastructure/server-side) signs the Jupiter swap transaction; Jito (execution) submits the signed transaction as a bundle.

relationships.description: Frontend SDKs provide UI components and hooks that wrap wallet infrastructure. The frontend SDK renders wallet interactions; the wallet infrastructure manages the keys.
relationships.workflow_context: OnchainKit (frontend-sdk) renders the wallet UI and transaction components. Privy (wallet-infrastructure) manages the actual embedded wallet and signing. OnchainKit wraps Privy — it does not replace it.

relationships.description: Frontend SDK hooks (wagmi, etc.) abstract over chain-data RPC calls, making them accessible as React state. The underlying data source is still an RPC provider.
relationships.workflow_context: wagmi (frontend-sdk) provides useBalance, useTransaction hooks. Under the hood, these hooks call an Alchemy or QuickNode (chain-data) RPC endpoint.

relationships.description: Workflow orchestration systems manage the lifecycle of agent runs — triggering execution, handling retries, surfacing step-by-step logs. The orchestration layer doesn't reason; it manages when and how the agent reasons.
relationships.workflow_context: In a production trading agent: Trigger.dev (workflow-orchestration) receives a Helius webhook, triggers the agent run, and manages retry if the agent step fails. The Vercel AI SDK agent (agent-framework) is what actually reasons within each step.

relationships.description: Context protocol implementations (MCP servers, skill files) expose wallet infrastructure tools' capabilities and APIs to AI coding agents, enabling agents to recommend and integrate them correctly.
Context protocols expose chain-data tool documentation to AI agents — Helius skill files, Base MCP's RPC context — enabling accurate code generation for blockchain data access.
DeFi protocol skill files (Jupiter official skill, ETHSkills DeFi coverage) give AI agents accurate API knowledge for integrating DeFi protocols.
Skill files for agent frameworks (sendaifun skills, ETHSkills orchestration patterns) teach AI agents how to build other AI agents correctly — the meta-use case.
Farcaster social auth (FID verification, custody address) feeds into wallet layer when building Farcaster apps — the social identity is the entry point for wallet association.
relationships.workflow_context: In a Farcaster miniapp: Neynar (social-layer) provides the FID and verified Ethereum address; Privy (wallet-infrastructure) creates or retrieves the embedded wallet for that identity.

relationships.description: Onchain identity protocols (ENS, Basenames, SIWE) resolve human-readable names and session proofs that map to the underlying wallet addresses managed by wallet infrastructure.
relationships.workflow_context: SIWE (identity) provides an auth session token. Privy (wallet-infrastructure) or reown (wallet-infrastructure) manages the wallet that signed the SIWE message.

relationships.description: Smart account wallets execute DeFi protocol operations with programmable rules — batched transactions, session keys that limit DeFi actions, automated protocol interactions without per-transaction user approval.
relationships.workflow_context: In a gasless DeFi app: a ZeroDev smart account (account-abstraction) executes a Uniswap swap (defi-protocol) in a single batched UserOperation with gas sponsored by a paymaster.

relationships.description: AI agent frameworks decide what transaction to construct and execute; wallet infrastructure performs the actual cryptographic signing. The agent owns the reasoning; the wallet owns the key. This is the fundamental separation of concerns in autonomous agent stacks — agent-framework must never directly hold or access private keys.
relationships.workflow_context: In an autonomous trading agent: Vercel AI SDK (agent-framework) determines a swap is warranted and constructs the transaction parameters; Turnkey (wallet-infrastructure/server-side) signs the constructed transaction. The agent cannot sign without the wallet layer.

relationships.description: Chain data webhooks (Alchemy, Helius) deliver onchain event triggers that activate workflow orchestration jobs. The event is the signal; the orchestrator durably executes the agent response to that signal. This relationship is the architectural backbone of all event-driven agent workflows.
relationships.workflow_context: In a Base AI agent: Alchemy (chain-data) delivers an address activity webhook to a Trigger.dev endpoint; Trigger.dev (workflow-orchestration) receives the event and starts a durable agent job that handles retries, step logging, and failure recovery.

relationships.description: Account abstraction bundlers read chain state (nonce, account deployment status, UserOp simulation results) before submitting UserOperations to the mempool. Bundlers are consumers of chain-data RPC APIs, not just abstract infrastructure.
relationships.workflow_context: In a gasless onboarding flow: Pimlico (account-abstraction) calls Alchemy (chain-data) RPC endpoints to check smart account deployment status, simulate the UserOperation for gas estimation, and submit the UserOp to the Base mempool.
